newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Fernandez sees no Brazil devaluation.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Fernandez sees no Brazil devaluation.

text.p: Argentine Economy Minister Roque Fernandez said Tuesday he did not expect Brazil to devalue its currency.
"I think that Brazil will not devalue," Fernandez said in an interview published in the new business daily Buenos Aires Economico. "It will continue with its current trade policy."
Fernandez said he also does not think Brazil will introduce any trade policies that will hit its Mercosur trade partners. The Mercosur customs union groups Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay.

"I do not think (Brazil) will generate problems of trade policies for Mercosur. We have managed to introduce respect in all the countries for Mercosur norms, so I do not think they will resolve any kind of problems with trade limitations," said Fernandez.
Turning to domestic issues, Fernandez promised he would not give in to the CGT labor federation in talks on labor market reforms. "I refuse to give in to the CGT," he said.

The government and the CGT have reached an agreement on labor market reforms, but the government wants to reach a compromise so the country's major business lobbies give their blessing to the deal as well.
Fernandez said the government is not going to be pushed into a labor market reform agreement because of political pressure ahead of October's mid-term congressional elections.
He confirmed that the government will not be able to reduce payroll taxes this year or in 1998, despite the view of many economists that such a step could help boost employment.
